name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah was a male Levite who served as a gatekeeper stationed on the north side, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:14. He was the son of Meshelemiah, also known as Shallum, which situates him within the Levitical duties related to temple service. His role as a gatekeeper highlights his responsibility in guarding the temple entrances during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means 'YHWH remembers,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that emphasizes God's faithfulness and remembrance of His people. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 9:21 and was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Zechariah is explicitly identified as the son of Shallum (Meshelemiah) in 1 Chronicles 9:21. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record any additional family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance lies in his Levitical role as a gatekeeper, a vital function in maintaining the sanctity and order of the temple. His stationing on the north gate, as indicated in 1 Chronicles 26:14, underscores the organized structure of temple service after the exile. Through his service, Zechariah contributed to the worship and preservation of the covenant community, embodying faithful stewardship of God's house.
